notes: Simplified reaction taxonomy using direct motif mapping and global motif groups from compound_logic.json.

reaction_types.description: Pd-catalyzed borylation of aryl/vinyl electrophiles to form boronate esters (Miyaura borylation).
Direct C-H borylation of arenes/heteroarenes under iridium catalysis.
Aryl amination via C-N cross-coupling; named variants differ mainly by catalyst.
Aryl ether formation via C-O coupling; named variants differ mainly by catalyst.
Aryl thioether formation via C-S coupling; named variants differ mainly by catalyst.
N/O/S nucleophilic substitution on alkyl electrophiles (halides/sulfonates), covering SN2-like alkylation.
Interconversion of aromatic/heteroaromatic halides (Ar-X to Ar-Y; halogen exchange).
Interconversion of aliphatic/benzylic/allylic halides (R-X to R-Y).
Ring-closing metathesis (RCM) forming cyclic alkenes.
Cyclocondensation/annulation to quinazolinone-like pyrimidine cores.
Aromatic nitration.
Friedel-Crafts acylation.
Friedel-Crafts alkylation.
Conjugate (1,4-) addition of nucleophiles to activated alkenes (Michael acceptors).
Arylation of C-H acidic compounds (alpha to carbonyl or other EWG) with aryl electrophiles.
Alkyl carboxylic acids add to aromatic C-H sites (often electron-deficient heteroarenes such as pyridine).
Alpha-keto acids add to aromatic C-H sites to form aryl ketones (Minisci acylation).
Decarboxylative coupling with Ar-X-like sp2 electrophiles and carboxylic-acid-derived partners (analogous to Minisci radical generation, but with electrophilic Ar-X coupling partner).
Wittig/HWE-like olefination of carbonyls to C=C products, supported by C-P bond cleavage evidence.
Catalytic hydrogenation of alkene motifs to saturated products; typing allows reaction SMILES where H2 is omitted but still requires saturated product evidence.
Cu-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition forming triazole-like heteroaromatic products.
Selective oxidation of primary alcohols to aldehydes.
Oxidation of secondary alcohols to ketones.
Over-oxidation of primary alcohols to carboxylic acids.
Benzylic C-H oxidation to aldehyde or ketone products.
Deep benzylic C-H oxidation to benzoic-acid type products.
Oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids.
Oxidative oxygen insertion of ketones to esters/lactones (Baeyer-Villiger).
Oxidative C=C cleavage delivering aldehyde/ketone fragments.
Strong oxidative C=C cleavage delivering carboxylic-acid fragments.
Oxidation of thioethers to sulfones.
Reduction of aldehydes and ketones to alcohol products.
Reduction of imines to amines.
Reduction of nitriles to primary amines.
Reduction of esters to alcohol products.
Selective reduction of acyl halides to aldehydes (Rosenmund-type).
Halogenation of unsaturated motifs (vinylic/alkynyl halides); supports product-only CRK fallback.
Conversion of alcohols to alkyl halides (Appel/SOCl2/oxalyl chloride families).
Installation of CF3 group on aryl/heteroaryl/alkenyl substrates.
Oxidation of alkenes to epoxides.
Aldol addition/condensation forming beta-hydroxy carbonyl or alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl products.
Grignard reagent addition to carbonyls forming C-C bonds.
[4+2] cycloaddition of diene and dienophile forming cyclohexene products.
Simmons-Smith cyclopropanation of alkenes using zinc carbenoid reagents.
Pauson-Khand [2+2+1] cycloaddition of alkyne, alkene and CO forming cyclopentenones.
Intramolecular amide bond formation giving cyclic lactam.
Intramolecular esterification forming cyclic lactone.
Mitsunobu reaction: inversion of alcohol configuration under PPh3/DIAD.
Hydrolysis of nitriles to carboxylic acids or amides.
Dihydroxylation of alkenes to syn or anti diols.
Protection of amines as Boc (tert-butoxycarbonyl) carbamates.
Protection of amines as Cbz (benzyloxycarbonyl) carbamates.
Protection of alcohols as silyl ethers (TMS, TBS, TIPS, TBDPS).
Sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chlorides and amines.
Carbamate formation from amines and chloroformates.
Gabriel synthesis: phthalimide alkylation then hydrazinolysis giving primary amines.
Curtius or Hofmann rearrangement: carboxylic acid to amine with loss of CO2.
Pd-catalyzed oxidation of terminal alkenes to methyl ketones (Wacker).
Diazotransfer converting primary amines to organic azides.
Nozaki-Hiyama-Kishi (NHK) reaction: Cr/Ni mediated coupling of vinyl halides with aldehydes.
Knoevenagel condensation of aldehydes with active methylene compounds.
Conversion of ketones/enolates to vinyl triflates for cross-coupling.
Synthesis of potassium aryltrifluoroborates from aryl halides.
Urea or thiourea formation from isocyanates/isothiocyanates and amines.
Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) activated by electron-withdrawing ring substituents.
Electrophilic fluorination using Selectfluor, NFSI or similar N-F reagents.
Pd-catalyzed Liebeskind-Srogl coupling of thioethers with boronic acids.
Giese radical addition to electron-deficient alkenes.
Radical or photoredox thiol-ene addition across alkenes.
